app.name: KESMA
app.tagline: Visualize, divide and compare land-division scenarios
app.disclaimerShort: Planning and visualization tool — not a legal, cadastral or valuation instrument.

disclaimer.title: Before you start
disclaimer.body1: KESMA helps families and professionals visualize, measure and compare possible land divisions.
disclaimer.body2: It does not determine legal inheritance rights, ownership, official cadastral boundaries or official land values. Any final division must be validated by the competent professionals (surveyor, notary, lawyer) and authorities.
disclaimer.body3: Your data stays on this device: nothing is sent to a server. Export your projects regularly to keep a backup.

guide.title: User guide
guide.intro: KESMA helps a family or a professional draw, measure and compare possible divisions of a property. Everything happens in your browser: no account, no server.
guide.tryDemo: The fastest way to discover it: on the home page, click “Try a demo”.

sections.title: 1. Add the property
items: Import a file: GeoJSON, KML/KMZ, zipped Shapefile, GPX or a CSV of corner points. Projected coordinates (e.g. Carthage / UTM) are detected and converted.
Or draw the parcels on the satellite map: click each corner, double-click or press Enter to finish.
Each parcel keeps its own name, land use, water access and notes. Parcels are never modified by scenarios.

sections.title: 2. Enter the heirs and their shares
items: A share can be a fraction (1/8, 7/24…), a percentage, a target area, or a part of the remainder with a weight (e.g. 2 for a son and 1 for a daughter).
Fractions stay exact. The summary shows when the shares do not add up to the whole property.
KESMA does not compute inheritance rights: enter the shares decided by the family or the notary.

sections.title: 3. Create division scenarios
items: Start from the parcels, from scratch, or use the automatic split: parallel strips by area or by value, in the order and direction you choose.
Edit lots on the map: cut with a line, merge, draw a lot, drag corners (shared edges move together), add or remove corners. Lots cannot leave the property.
Assign each lot to a beneficiary, lock lots you agree on, and save named versions to come back to later.

sections.title: 4. Value and road access (optional)
items: Set a base value per m², draw value zones (irrigated land, building land…), and add assets such as wells, buildings or orchards.
Draw the roads along the property: each lot's road frontage is measured, and a lot has access with at least 3 m of frontage.
Values are estimates you enter yourself — not official valuations.

sections.title: 5. Check the scenario
items: Allocation compares what each beneficiary receives with their target, by area or by value, against the tolerance set in the project settings.
Validation finds overlaps, gaps, parts outside the property, invalid shapes and unassigned lots, and offers one-click fixes.

sections.title: 6. Compare, report and export
items: Compare scenarios shows two synchronised maps and a table of indicators (deviations, road access, fragmentation…).
The report is a printable A4 document (plans, tables, validation, notes, disclaimer on every page): print it or save it as PDF.
Exports: project file (.kesma.json) to share or back up, GeoJSON for GIS software (QGIS…), Excel and CSV tables.

sections.title: 7. Your data
items: Projects are saved automatically in this browser only. Clearing browser data deletes them: export the project file regularly.
To work on another computer or share with a relative, send the .kesma.json file and import it from the home page.
Undo / redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) keep the last 100 changes of the open project.

guide.limits: KESMA is a planning and visualization tool. Areas are computed on the ellipsoid and are accurate for planning, but the tool does not replace a surveyor, a notary or the land registry. Any final division must be validated by the competent professionals and authorities.
